stations.name: Dakshin Gangotri
stations.location: Princess Astrid Coast, Queen Maud Land, East Antarctica

timeline.historic_status: Antarctic Treaty Historic Site and Monument No. 44

engineering.structure: Two-storey prefabricated timber container structure mounted on heavy wooden skids
engineering.water_system: Sub-surface snow melting tank using generator exhaust waste heat recovery

scientific_facilities: Automatic Weather Station recording surface wind, air temperature, and solar flux
Fluxgate magnetometer for auroral electrojet magnetic field observations
HF radio communication array with New Delhi
stations.historical_significance: India's first permanent Antarctic base, erected in a record 60 days during the 3rd Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica led by Dr. H.K. Srivastava.

stations.name: Maitri
stations.location: Schirmacher Oasis, Queen Maud Land, East Antarctica

engineering.structure: Elevated steel-stilt modular superstructure with insulated polyurethane sandwich panels
engineering.power_generation: Multiple Volvo Penta diesel generators with heat exchangers
engineering.heating: Circulating closed-loop glycol water heating system
engineering.water_supply: Lake Priyadarshini freshwater lake with thermally traced intake line

scientific_facilities: Surface Meteorology & Atmospheric Radiation Suite (AWS, Kipp & Zonen pyranometers)
Brewer Spectrophotometer (Total Column Ozone and UV-B index)
Ozonesonde Balloon Sounding System
Geomagnetism & Space Weather Laboratory (CSIR-NGRI Digital Fluxgate Magnetometer, Riometer, VLF whistler receiver)
Permanent IGS GPS Tracking Station for Antarctic plate tectonic drift
Cold Microbiology & Limnology Laboratory with incubators and autoclaves
Human Physiology and Isolation Adaptation Lab
stations.historical_significance: Second permanent base, continuously manned for over 35 years without a single day of shutdown. Built during the 8th ISEA led by Dr. R. Sengupta.

stations.name: Bharati
stations.location: Grovnes Peninsula, Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica

coordinates.terrain: Coastal granitic bedrock and paragneiss hills

engineering.structure: Aerodynamic double-skin container modular envelope elevated on pilings to shed 200 km/h blizzard winds
engineering.power_generation: Cogeneration Combined Heat and Power (CHP) plant with thermal recovery
engineering.environmental_systems: Membrane bioreactor (MBR) zero-effluent wastewater recycling plant discharging pure greywater

scientific_facilities: ISRO / NRSC Antarctica Ground Station (AGS) tracking Indian Earth Observation Satellites (Oceansat, Cartosat, Resourcesat)
Walk-in -20°C Ice Core Processing and Cold Storage Laboratory
Oceanographic and Marine Biology Wet Lab with sea-ice sampling equipment
Atmospheric Physics & Aerosol Observatory (Aethalometer, Nephelometer, Sun Photometer)
High-Resolution Coastal Automatic Weather Station
stations.historical_significance: Commissioned during the 31st ISEA. India became one of only a handful of nations operating multiple modern year-round Antarctic research stations.

stations.name: Himadri

engineering.structure: Renovated historical Arctic timber building conforming to Kings Bay AS conservation guidelines
engineering.power_supply: Ny-Ålesund village microgrid powered by district cogeneration

scientific_facilities: Aerosol Physics Suite at Gruvebadet Clean Atmospheric Laboratory
Magee Scientific AE-33 7-wavelength Aethalometer for Black Carbon
METEK Micro Rain Radar-2 (MRR) for boundary layer precipitation dynamics
OTT PARSIVEL Optical Laser Disdrometer for hydrometeor size spectra
Glacier Mass Balance field stations at Vestre Lovénbreen and Austre Brøggerbreen
Marine Fjord Ecology Lab investigating Kongsfjorden pelagic ecosystem
stations.historical_significance: Inaugurated on 1 July 2008, establishing India as the 11th country with a permanent research base at the world's northernmost scientific settlement.

stations.name: IndARC Moored Observatory

timeline.service_interval: Annual recovery, sensor recalibration, data download, and redeployment

sensor_payload: Seabird SBE-37 MicroCAT CTD sensors at multiple depths (temp, conductivity, depth)
Aanderaa SeaGuard Recording Doppler Current Profiler (RDCP)
WetLabs ECO-FLNTU combination fluorometer and optical turbidity sensor
Acoustic release transponders for retrieval triggering
stations.historical_significance: India's first multi-sensor subsurface moored observatory deployed in the high Arctic. Tracks seasonal intrusion of warm Atlantic Water into the Arctic fjord system.

stations.name: Himansh
stations.location: Sutri Dhaka, Chandra Basin, Lahaul-Spiti, Himachal Pradesh

timeline.status: Operational (Seasonal April to November plus automated winter logging)

engineering.structure: Specially insulated weather-proof containerized modules engineered for sub-zero temperatures and high wind loads
engineering.power_supply: Solar photovoltaic hybrid system backed up by silent diesel generators

scientific_facilities: High-altitude Campbell Scientific Automated Weather Station (AWS)
Leica Viva Differential Global Positioning System (DGPS) for ice velocity
Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) for ice depth and bed topography profiling
Network of glaciological ablation stakes across Sutri Dhaka, Batal, and Samudra Tapu glaciers
Cryogenic and refrigerated storage for glacial ice and water chemistry samples
stations.historical_significance: India's dedicated high-altitude research station monitoring the Himalayan Cryosphere ('The Third Pole'), which feeds major South Asian river systems.

vessels.name: ORV Sagar Kanya
vessels.owner: Ministry of Earth Sciences, Govt. of India
capabilities: 24-bottle CTD rosette with deep-sea hydrographic winch (up to 6000 m)
Piston and gravity corers for sediment recovery
vessels.polar_role: Chartered flagship vessel that conducted the landmark pilot Indian Southern Ocean Expedition in 2004.

vessels.name: ORV Sagar Nidhi
vessels.owner: National Institute of Ocean Technology / MoES
vessels.ice_classification: Ice-strengthened hull (classified for operations in floating polar ice up to 0.4 m)
capabilities: Launch and recovery systems for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) and ROVs
Deep-water CTD, deep sub-bottom profiler, marine meteorological station
vessels.polar_role: Operates multi-disciplinary cruises in sub-Antarctic and Southern Ocean waters investigating carbon fluxes.
